headline: 3,000 Get Sight Back in Caribbean Surgical Marathon
meta_description: US-Caribbean churches organized a 12-day surgical marathon in Trinidad and Tobago, restoring free cataract surgery to 3,000 people who had waited years.
summary_short: In a 12-day surgical marathon at a hospital in Cocorite, Trinidad and Tobago, 3,000 people regained their vision through free cataract and pterygium surgery.
body:
Between May 14th and 26th, volunteer surgeons performed 3,000 free eye surgeries at a community hospital in Cocorite, Trinidad and Tobago, thanks to a partnership between the Church of the 7th Day Adventists, Hands International, and Eyes for India. Many patients had waited years for cataract surgery or never had access due to cost. The breakthrough came through a high-volume surgical technique that enabled the team to perform 450 procedures daily—allowing hundreds of islanders to regain sharp vision, improved night sight, and restored quality of life.

The surgical marathon addressed a critical need. "When we replace that lens, people see again. Colors become sharper. Night blindness improves. It changes quality of life," explained Reynold Agard, the Tobago-born president of Hands International. Beyond cataracts, the initiative also treated pterygium—commonly called "surfer's eye"—a non-cancerous growth linked to ultraviolet exposure, dust, and wind.

The biggest logistical challenge wasn't the surgeries themselves, but the screening process. Most patients arrived without pre-surgical screening simply because they couldn't afford it. Volunteers had to quickly divide the patient queue into those already screened and those needing assessment before surgery. Despite this obstacle, the minimally invasive procedures enabled rapid improvements in eyesight and quick hospital discharge. For Alexander Isaac, health ministries director for the Caribbean Union Conference, the effort reflected deeper purpose: "Healthcare ministry remains one of the most effective ways for the church to engage communities and reveal Christ's love in practical ways."
